lane-3.evidence_quality: Genuinely double-edged. Re-ran real instruments (t13_probe.py census/sanity/replay, `zig test src/colex.zig`) and its stated verdict convention is the most explicit and self-aware in the field ('verified' means the row's status is correct at HEAD; 'refuted' would mean the status/substance is wrong). It DID find T372's contrast probe and cited it correctly for both G01 and G10 — substantively matching lane-1's core catch on those two claims — but chose to keep the verdict label 'verified' rather than 'refuted', reasoning that promotion/correction 'is the operator's call'. That choice is defensible as a convention but it is exactly the labelling gap this round exists to expose: a reader scanning verdicts alone would not learn that G01/G10's stated rationale is stale. Missed G06 (no primary per-seat report check), G07 (treated the gate as literally mechanized, no pre-commit/build.zig check), G12/G13/G20 (no T473/T212/T383), and never used 'unverifiable-at-head' even where warranted (G18).

Its lower false-verified count (6, vs 9 for lanes 2/3/5) is largely a labelling artifact: lane-4 defaults FALSE-type rows to a 'refuted' verdict (matching the register, not a new finding) rather than genuinely interrogating PROVEN/CLAIMED rows, so it happens to dodge the false-verified trap on claims it was never at risk of mis-verifying in the first place, while still missing every one of the batch's ten real staleness/overclaim problems on the PROVEN/CLAIMED side (G06, G07, G12, G13, G16, G17, G18, G20 all graded 'verified, no change').

complementarity.note: Ruling 34: correctness against my own per-claim ruling matters far more here than pairwise agreement — lanes 2/3/5 agree with each other on 23-24/25 claims precisely because they share the same rubber-stamp failure mode (see lane_scores), not because they are independently correct. High mutual agreement among the rubber-stamps should not be read as corroboration.

best_pair_by_agreement.caveat: tied with lane-3/lane-5 at 24/25 (see matrix); this is the agreement-among-rubber-stamps pair, not the most-correct pair — the most-correct lane (lane-1) has the LOWEST pairwise agreement with every other lane (13-14/25) because it is the one lane that dissents from the shared blind spot.

nuance.lane-1: First, clearly. 23/25 correct, ZERO false-verifieds (the only lane with none), 8 uniquely-correct calls no other lane made, and the only lane whose G06 finding required opening a primary per-seat report (not just the synthesizing ADR) to catch a real discrepancy between that report and its own decision doc's summary.

nuance.lane-2: Fourth. 15/25 correct on paper (tied with lane-5) but the shallowest of the three middle lanes in substance: missed T372 on the single highest-dependent claim in the batch (G01, 9 dependents) entirely, and used 'unverifiable-at-head' as a dodge on a claim (G05) that is straightforwardly verifiable.
nuance.lane-4: Fifth. 13/25 correct, the thinnest file by a wide margin (8x smaller than lane-1), no independent reproduction anywhere, and one real analytical misstep (proposing a status change on G10 that the row's own text explicitly forbids). Its lower false-verified count is a labelling artifact, not rigor — see lane_scores.

ranking.bet: lane-1 over the field: ~90-95% — the zero-false-verified record and 8 unique correct calls are each independently primary-source-verified by me (T372, T378, T473, T212, T383, and the Kimi report divergence all exist exactly as lane-1 describes them; I did not take lane-1's word for any of them). lane-3 vs lane-5 for second: a genuine tie, call it 55-45 either way — lane-3 has one more strict-correct claim and zero non-conforming entries, lane-5 has more granular citation-drift catches and one more uniquely-sourced observation (G14); a rerun could plausibly flip this rung. lane-5 vs lane-2 for third/fourth: ~65% lane-5, on substantive depth (T372 found) despite an identical correct-count. lane-2 over lane-4: ~80%, on file depth and the avoidance of lane-4's G10 misstep.
